=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel — Buyer-Side Review of Seller Positions

Baseline reminders: price AUD 24m, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law. Below, each issue gives the Seller's position, the buyer's objective, and my recommendation.

---

**SPA-N-001 — General liability cap**
- *Seller:* 20% of price = AUD 4.8m aggregate cap on general Warranty Claims.
- *Buyer wants:* Higher cap (commonly 30–50% for general warranties; 100%+ for fundamentals/tax).
- *Recommendation:* **Push to ≥30–50% for general warranties; reject this applying to fundamental/title/tax.** Reason: 20% is low given concentrated customer/IP/privacy risk here.

**SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k basket; recover only excess above basket.
- *Buyer wants:* Lower thresholds and a **first-dollar ("tipping") basket**, not excess-only.
- *Recommendation:* **Accept modest de minimis; convert basket to tipping-basket and resist excess-only.** Reason: excess-only basket effectively gifts Seller the first AUD 250k of valid claims.

**SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* 18 months post-Completion; and the catch-all default that any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise.
- *Buyer wants:* Minimum 24 months (through at least two audit cycles); reject the "applies to all Claims" default.
- *Recommendation:* **Seek 24 months; strike the blanket catch-all.** Reason: 18 months may expire before first full-year audit surfaces issues; the catch-all silently sweeps fundamentals/tax/fraud into short limits.

**SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity and title warranties subject to **same cap and time limits** as general ("administrative simplicity").
- *Buyer wants:* Fundamentals/title at **100% of price** (or uncapped) with **long/statutory limitation** (6–7 years).
- *Recommendation:* **Reject outright — carve fundamentals/title out of the general cap and short clock.** Reason: if title fails, buyer could lose the whole company but recover only AUD 4.8m.

**SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* Silent — and Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 purport to apply limitations/exclusive-remedy/non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature."
- *Buyer wants:* Express carve-out so **no cap, time limit, basket, knowledge or non-reliance bar** applies to fraud, wilful default or fraudulent misrepresentation.
- *Recommendation:* **Insist on an explicit fraud carve-out across all limitation clauses.** Reason: "all Claims of any nature" would otherwise try to cap even fraud — commercially and arguably legally unacceptable.

**SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* General disclosure of the **entire data room and all public registers** (deemed disclosure of everything).
- *Buyer wants:* Disclosure limited to matters **fairly and specifically disclosed in sufficient detail** to identify the nature/scope of the issue.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject blanket/sweep-up disclosure; require "fair disclosure" standard with specific cross-referencing.** Reason: dumping a data room should not immunise Seller against warranties for issues buyer couldn't reasonably identify.

**SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- *Seller:* No claim for any matter buyer/advisers had knowledge of, **including anything discoverable** from data room or public records (constructive knowledge).
- *Buyer wants:* No knowledge bar at all; at most **actual knowledge of specified individuals**, never "discoverable/constructive."
- *Recommendation:* **Strike "discoverable"; limit to actual knowledge of named deal-team members (or delete entirely).** Reason: constructive-knowledge bar penalises diligence and guts the warranties.

**SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent (~AUD 3.6m / ~30% revenue)**
- *Seller:* "Reasonable endeavours"; treat consent as satisfied **on delivery of counterparty's written consent**; no final consent yet provided, conditions unsatisfied.
- *Buyer wants:* **Condition precedent** — unconditional written consent (and satisfaction of cl.11.3 conditions) delivered **before Completion**.
- *Recommendation:* **Make Bluefen consent a hard CP to Completion, not a post-closing endeavour.** Reason: loss of a ~30% customer on change-of-control is a material value risk — must be resolved pre-close or priced.

**SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m)**
- *Seller:* Release/discharge to be provided **following Completion**; not yet repaid.
- *Buyer wants:* On a debt-free/cash-free deal, debt **repaid and security discharged at Completion** out of proceeds (via funds flow).
- *Recommendation:* **Require payoff letter and discharge of security at Completion; reflect in funds flow.** Reason: post-closing release leaves buyer owning encumbered company with residual security — inconsistent with debt-free basis.

**SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses (AUD 420k)**
- *Seller:* "Matter for the Seller"; DD-005 Completion bonuses **not in funds flow**; on-costs (payroll tax/super) unaddressed.
- *Buyer wants:* These are **Seller/pre-Completion liabilities** (triggered by Completion) — borne by Seller or deducted at close, **including on-costs**.
- *Recommendation:* **Add to funds flow as Seller cost (gross of super/payroll tax) or specific indemnity.** Reason: Completion-triggered bonuses are leakage; on debt-free/cash-free basis they are Seller's, not buyer's post-close burden.

**SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity (AUD 180k open)**
- *Seller:* Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "adequate." Payment/assignment unconfirmed; SOW3 Project Materials only transfer on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees.
- *Buyer wants:* Confirmation of **payment AND confirmatory IP assignment** pre-Completion, or a **full specific indemnity** covering loss of IP rights, not just the fee.
- *Recommendation:* **Require proof of payment + assignment as CP, or broaden indemnity beyond the fee to cover IP title loss/consequential loss.** Reason: if fees unpaid, buyer may not own SOW3 IP at all — capping at the fee understates exposure.

**SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident (DD-006, ~1,240 records)**
- *Seller:* "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material; no confirmed breach; no loss stated.
- *Buyer wants:* Full disclosure of scope, **specific indemnity** for notification/regulatory costs/fines/third-party claims, and interim conduct/cooperation covenants.
- *Recommendation:* **Treat as live risk — demand specific indemnity (uncapped or separately capped) plus investigation update before signing.** Reason: potential Privacy Act notifiable data breach (OAIC); regulatory/penalty exposure far exceeds "not material" framing.

**SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k, 3 × 110k)**
- *Seller:* "Ordinary-course operating costs"; doesn't say if unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- *Buyer wants:* Clarity on whether these are **committed liabilities/leakage** and whether structured (split into 3×110k) to dodge a threshold.
- *Recommendation:* **Diligence the three together; confirm termination rights and treat committed amounts as debt-like/leakage if pre-Completion.** Reason: the 3×110k structure may be engineered to sit under review thresholds; aggregate is material.

**SPA-N-014 — Category separation**
- *Seller:* Single regime — same cap/time limits/basket/exclusions apply to **all Claims** (general, fundamental, title, tax, indemnities).
- *Buyer wants:* **Tiered regime** — separate (higher/longer) treatment for fundamentals, title, tax and specific indemnities; indemnities outside the basket.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject single-bucket; insist on category separation with carve-outs for indemnity claims from basket/cap.** Reason: collapsing categories lets short general limits swallow the high-value protections.

**SPA-N-015 — Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012; notes buyer hasn't verified.
- *Buyer wants:* **Full title warranty** (unencumbered legal and beneficial ownership of 100%) backed by independent verification (ASIC search, register, share certificates, no security interests/PPSR).
- *Recommendation:* **Do not rely on Seller's register alone — require title warranty + independent PPSR/ASIC checks; title warranty uncapped.** Reason: register is Seller-controlled evidence; buyer needs an independent, warranted chain of title.

**SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" (i.e., general cap/18-month/basket).
- *Buyer wants:* **Dedicated tax covenant/deed** (statutory limitation period ~7 yrs, no basket) and **IP warranties** with longer survival and higher cap.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject folding tax/IP into general regime; negotiate a separate tax deed and enhanced IP warranty suite.** Reason: tax has long statutory tails and IP is core value — both need protection beyond the 18-month/AUD 4.8m general cap.

---

### Cross-cutting priorities (negotiation hierarchy)
1. **Fundamentals/title/tax/fraud carve-outs** (001, 004, 005, 014, 016) — non-negotiable structural protections.
2. **Deal-breaker CPs**: Bluefen consent (008) and Riverlark discharge (009) before Completion.
3. **Specific indemnities**: privacy incident (012) and Ironquay (011).
4. **Leakage/funds-flow**: bonuses (010) and Sandbar (013) — adjust price/funds flow.
5. **Erosion mechanics**: basket (002), knowledge (007), disclosure scope (006).

Want me to turn this into a markup/issues list for the SPA or a priority term sheet for the negotiation call?
